title: Painting: Watching the Robot You Wrote in Phase 00 Drive

questions.question: When should a widget do its drawing?
options: Whenever the data changes, from any function
In a timer running at the screen refresh rate
Inside paintEvent, which Qt calls when the pixels are needed
Once, in the constructor
questions.explanation: Qt asks the widget to draw itself. Painting anywhere else either does nothing or flickers, and it is the first thing to check when a custom widget misbehaves.

questions.question: What does update() do?
options: Recomputes the widget's layout
Asks for a repaint soon, collapsing several requests into one
Paints the widget immediately
Forces every widget in the window to redraw
questions.explanation: Requests coalesce, so a control loop running at a kilohertz can call update freely without producing a thousand repaints a second.

questions.question: Why does mapping a pose to a pixel involve subtracting from the widget height?
options: To centre the path vertically
The robot's y grows upward and the widget's y grows downward
Because the margin is measured from the bottom
Because pixel coordinates cannot be negative
questions.explanation: The flip converts a distance above the bottom into a distance below the top. Leaving it out draws a mirror image that looks plausible enough to miss.

questions.question: Why does the mapping use one scale for both axes rather than fitting each separately?
options: So the shape is not distorted when the window is not square
Because Qt only accepts a single scale
Because two scales would be slower
To keep the margin equal on all sides
questions.explanation: Fitting each axis independently would stretch a circular path into an ellipse, which misrepresents what the robot actually did.

questions.question: How can a widget be tested without a screen?
options: Take a screenshot of the desktop
Widgets cannot be tested without a display
Compare the source code against a known good version
Render it into a QImage and inspect the pixels, with the offscreen platform plugin
questions.explanation: render draws into any paint device, so the test can ask real questions of the result and run on a machine with no display at all.

questions.question: Why does this lesson not claim support on Windows?
options: This repository's continuous integration does not build Qt there, and an unproven claim is worth less than none
Because QPainter is Linux only
Because the offscreen platform plugin is unavailable there
Qt Widgets do not work on Windows
questions.explanation: The code would very likely work. The rule is that a platform is claimed only when it is proven, so the claim would be added at the same time as the CI lane that verifies it.
